tldr: Normalized importance attributes treatment-effect variation to a removed covariate, and its uncertainty can remain large when total heterogeneity shrinks. For the full uniform-square Bernoulli observational shell \(D(P)\in[\rho^2,2\rho^2]\), with one-tenth Hölder propensity and baseline response and a Lipschitz CATE, the proved critical sequence is \(b_n=n^{-2/13}\), with no logarithmic multiplier. Uniformly honest expected interval length vanishes if and only if \(\rho_n/b_n\to\infty\), for every deterministic shell sequence. The explicit total interval uses original-record pair moments, coarse spatial inverses, crossed projection energies and finite polygon inversion; its coverage is at least \(9/10\) at every sample size. Explicit same-shell priors and their original-record likelihood comparison prove the converse. The finite-sample bracket is \(c_{\mathrm{low}}\min\{1,a_n^2/\rho^2\}\le L_n(\rho)\le2^{34}\min\{1,a_n/\rho\}\), where \(a_n=n^{-2/13}\) and \(c_{\mathrm{low}}=3/(5\cdot2^{2050})\). These width orders remain unmatched: the vanishing-length boundary is exact, while sharp width away from that boundary is not claimed. The full shell retains exact importance zero, one and every interior value, as well as unrestricted mean effects subject to its primitive conditions.
gap: Fixed-law normalized-importance asymptotics in \cite{HinesDiazOrdazVansteelandt2025} do not answer when uniformly honest uncertainty can vanish over shrinking positive shells with rough observational confounding. The closest local upper construction leaves its rough-regime likelihood converse unresolved.
fill: An evaluated original-record interval and an explicit continuous-frame same-shell likelihood construction would give the two directions of the consistency criterion, including arbitrary nonmonotone shell sequences. The decisive construction must establish every supported law's legality, deterministic target separation and a uniform finite-sample total-variation bound with evaluated constants.
